title: Strict chain representatives for ordinal derived descent data
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\lambda$ be a set-sized ordinal, and let $(W_\alpha)_{\alpha<\lambda}$ be increasing opens of $X$ with $W_\alpha=\bigcup_{\beta<\alpha}W_\beta$ at every non-successor $\alpha<\lambda$, including $W_0=\varnothing$ when $\lambda>0$. A covering of $X$ is not required. Let $K_\alpha\in D(\mathcal O_{W_\alpha})$ [def-pc-derived-category] satisfy $\operatorname{Hom}(K_\alpha,K_\alpha[i])=0$ for every $i<0$. Suppose isomorphisms $r_\beta^\alpha:K_\alpha|_{W_\beta}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_\beta$ are given for all $\beta<\alpha<\lambda$ and satisfy $r_\gamma^\alpha=r_\gamma^\beta\circ(r_\beta^\alpha|_{W_\gamma})$ for $\gamma<\beta<\alpha$. For each $\alpha$ fix any K-injective complex $I_\alpha$ of $\mathcal O_{W_\alpha}$-modules [def-pur-kinjective-complex] and an isomorphism $e_\alpha:QI_\alpha\xrightarrow{\sim}K_\alpha$, with $Q$ the derived localization. There exist quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] of complexes $f_{\beta\alpha}:I_\beta\to I_\alpha|_{W_\beta}$ such that $f_{\gamma\alpha}=(f_{\beta\alpha}|_{W_\gamma})\circ f_{\gamma\beta}$ as chain maps for every $\gamma<\beta<\alpha$, and $Q(f_{\beta\alpha})=(e_\alpha|_{W_\beta})^{-1}\circ(r_\beta^\alpha)^{-1}\circ e_\beta$ in $D(\mathcal O_{W_\beta})$ for every $\beta<\alpha$. Here restriction of a complex is termwise restriction, canonically identified after $Q$ with derived restriction.

source.place: Tag 0D6B (cohomology-lemma-glueing-increasing-union), proof, transfinite recursion on chosen K-injective representatives, successor composition and the limit comparison C to I_alpha (returned steps 1, 3, 7--8); comparison direction and uniqueness citation corrected as in the parent.

proof.text: Put $a_{\beta\alpha}=(e_\alpha|_{W_\beta})^{-1}(r_\beta^\alpha)^{-1}e_\beta$. The given cocycle implies $a_{\gamma\alpha}=(a_{\beta\alpha}|_{W_\gamma})a_{\gamma\beta}$. We construct, by transfinite recursion on $\alpha<\lambda$, all maps into index $\alpha$, retaining the earlier maps, with the two invariants $Q(f_{\beta\alpha})=a_{\beta\alpha}$ and strict triple composition. At index zero there are no maps to choose. On the site of opens of $W_\alpha$, the slice at $W_\beta$ is literally the site of opens contained in $W_\beta$, with the restricted structure sheaf. Thus [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized] makes $I_\alpha|_{W_\beta}$ K-injective. Choose a common universe containing the set of opens and the coefficient modules, so the module-size hypothesis of that lemma holds. Restriction sends a zero component to the same zero component, supplying its zero-morphism parameter. We will also use the following elementary consequence of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: if $Q(g)$ is invertible then each $H^q(g)$ is invertible, because $H^q$ factors through $Q$; hence $g$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Conversely $Q$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms by its definition.

source.place: Tag 0D6B (cohomology-lemma-glueing-increasing-union), transfinite recursion; limit comparison uses Tag 0D68 (cohomology-lemma-uniqueness), rather than the finite-case pointer printed in 0D6B.

proof.text: Suppose $\alpha=\delta+1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], applied to the source $I_\delta$ and the K-injective target $I_\alpha|_{W_\delta}$ from Step 1, choose a chain map $g:I_\delta\to I_\alpha|_{W_\delta}$ representing $a_{\delta\alpha}$. A morphism in the homotopy category is a homotopy class of chain maps, so the asserted surjectivity supplies an actual representative. Put $f_{\delta\alpha}=g$ and $f_{\beta\alpha}=(g|_{W_\beta})f_{\beta\delta}$ for $\beta<\delta$. The cocycle equation of Step 1 proves the prescribed derived class of every new map. Each is a quasi-isomorphism by the cohomology argument of Step 1. For $\gamma<\beta<\delta$, substitute the old equality $f_{\gamma\delta}=(f_{\beta\delta}|_{W_\gamma})f_{\gamma\beta}$ into this formula; associativity gives $f_{\gamma\alpha}=(f_{\beta\alpha}|_{W_\gamma})f_{\gamma\beta}$ strictly. The triple with $\beta=\delta$ is the defining formula itself.

source.place: Tag 0D6B (cohomology-lemma-glueing-increasing-union), transfinite recursion; limit comparison uses Tag 0D68 (cohomology-lemma-uniqueness), rather than the finite-case pointer printed in 0D6B.

proof.text: Suppose $\alpha$ is a nonzero limit and that all earlier maps have been constructed. Continuity gives the increasing cover $W_\alpha=\bigcup_{\beta<\alpha}W_\beta$. Apply [lem-trf-derived-strict-open-colimit] on this open subscheme, to the ordinal $\alpha$, the complexes $I_\beta$, and the earlier maps. All its quasi-isomorphism and strict-composition hypotheses are induction invariants. Obtain a complex $C$ on $W_\alpha$ and quasi-isomorphisms $s_\beta:I_\beta\to C|_{W_\beta}$ with $s_\gamma=(s_\beta|_{W_\gamma})f_{\gamma\beta}$. Write $M=QC$ and $N=QI_\alpha$. We must construct one derived map $M\to N$, before choosing a chain representative; individual lifts on the opens would supply only homotopy compatibility.

source.place: Tag 0D6B (cohomology-lemma-glueing-increasing-union), transfinite recursion; limit comparison uses Tag 0D68 (cohomology-lemma-uniqueness), rather than the finite-case pointer printed in 0D6B.

proof.text: Set $h_\beta=a_{\beta\alpha}Q(s_\beta)^{-1}:M|_{W_\beta}\xrightarrow{\sim}N|_{W_\beta}$. For $\gamma<\beta<\alpha$, the equations $a_{\gamma\alpha}=(a_{\beta\alpha}|_{W_\gamma})a_{\gamma\beta}$, $Q(f_{\gamma\beta})=a_{\gamma\beta}$ and $Q(s_\gamma)=(Q(s_\beta)|_{W_\gamma})Q(f_{\gamma\beta})$ give $h_\gamma=h_\beta|_{W_\gamma}$ by cancellation. Let $\mathcal C$ be the set of distinct opens among the $W_\beta$, $\beta<\alpha$. Equal opens receive equal maps by the same equation, using the order of their indices, so $h$ defines an inclusion-compatible family on $\mathcal C$. It covers $W_\alpha$ and refines intersections: the intersection of two members is the smaller member itself. On each $W_\beta$, the maps $e_\beta Q(s_\beta)^{-1}$ and $r_\beta^\alpha(e_\alpha|_{W_\beta})$ identify $M|_{W_\beta}$ and $N|_{W_\beta}$ with $K_\beta$. Conjugation, also after shifts, therefore identifies each negative Hom group for any of the ordered pairs $(M,N),(N,M),(M,M),(N,N)$ on this open with $\operatorname{Hom}(K_\beta,K_\beta[i])=0$.

source.place: Tag 0D6B (cohomology-lemma-glueing-increasing-union), transfinite recursion; limit comparison uses Tag 0D68 (cohomology-lemma-uniqueness), rather than the finite-case pointer printed in 0D6B.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-derived-basis-local-hom-glue] on $W_\alpha$, with covering collection $\mathcal C$, $O=W_\alpha$ and pair $(M,N)$. Step 4 checks precisely its intersection and local negative-Hom hypotheses. Its Hom bijection gives $u:M\to N$ restricting to every $h_\beta$. For $(N,M)$ it gives $v:N\to M$ restricting to $h_\beta^{-1}$. Apply the injective parts of the bijections for $(M,M)$ and $(N,N)$: the composites $vu$ and $uv$ restrict to the identities, so they equal the identities globally. Thus $u$ is an isomorphism, with $u|_{W_\beta}\,Q(s_\beta)=a_{\beta\alpha}$. This uses the general local-Hom uniqueness statement, not existence for a finite subcover; there need not be any finite subcover.

source.place: Tag 0D6B (cohomology-lemma-glueing-increasing-union), transfinite recursion; limit comparison uses Tag 0D68 (cohomology-lemma-uniqueness), rather than the finite-case pointer printed in 0D6B.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] for the source $C$ and the given K-injective target $I_\alpha$, choose a chain map $t:C\to I_\alpha$ with $Q(t)=u$. Define $f_{\beta\alpha}=(t|_{W_\beta})s_\beta$. Step 5 gives $Q(f_{\beta\alpha})=(u|_{W_\beta})Q(s_\beta)=a_{\beta\alpha}$, so these maps are quasi-isomorphisms by Step 1. Moreover the chain equality from Step 3 gives, without changing any earlier choice, $f_{\gamma\alpha}=(t|_{W_\gamma})s_\gamma=(t|_{W_\gamma})(s_\beta|_{W_\gamma})f_{\gamma\beta}=(f_{\beta\alpha}|_{W_\gamma})f_{\gamma\beta}$. This completes the limit extension with strict composition.

proof.text: The zero, successor and nonzero-limit cases extend the same partial system without changing its earlier maps, so set-sized transfinite recursion supplies all required $f_{\beta\alpha}$. For $\lambda=0$ or $1$ there are no pairs. Empty or repeated opens are allowed throughout; the Hom-gluing lemma includes the empty scheme, and Step 4 checks repetitions explicitly. Only covers of individual limit opens were used, so the family need not cover $X$. The complexes $I_\alpha$ and identifications $e_\alpha$ remain the prescribed ones.

No new nodes, no unit changes, and the statement is identical to every earlier Q88 snapshot. It is a plain one-level split, not a re-split order. Stacks 0D6B (cohomology.tex 11343-11455) matches the item's recursion: successor lift and compose, then at a limit a termwise colimit C and a chain map tau from C to I_alpha. The report's source corrections are right: Stacks writes tau as representing sigma : K_alpha -> C, which is the wrong direction, and it points to the finite-case lemma for uniqueness where the 0D68 global-Hom gluing argument is needed. Each cited statement says what the step takes from it. kinjective-restrict-localized: the slice over W_beta is canonically the site of opens of W_beta (a 'literally' that holds up to that identification). I accept it as a declared tool use; it is a generic lemma from unit sk-def-sf-operations. kinjective-hom-derived: Mathlib leaf; surjectivity for an arbitrary source into a K-injective target. strict-open-colimit: applied on the scheme W_alpha, which its earlier opens cover by continuity; it gives strict coprojections. basis-local-hom-glue: intersections of members are the smaller member; negative Hom holds by conjugation to K_beta. I recomputed the a-cocycle, the successor strictness, h_beta|_{W_gamma}=h_gamma, the inverse gluing (vu=1, uv=1 by injectivity) and the limit strictness (t|)s_gamma=(f_{beta alpha}|)f_{gamma beta}. Edge cases checked: lambda=0,1; W_0 empty; repeated opens; alpha=omega with no finite subcover; a family not covering X. No dependency cycle (only the parent increasing-union cites it), no duplicate found by rg, and no SGA source.
